refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: platformd-verifyd.service is a system service that challenges a user to prove presence and records the result. On request it runs the platformd-verify PAM stack for the calling user, and on success reports the verification to platformd-trustd.service8 so the session's freshness reflects it. It is requested with verifyctl1.

It is the challenger that complements the observer: platformd-trustd.service8 reports and attests the platform's authentication state, and this service re-establishes user presence on demand when a policy that needs recent verification has lapsed. It never asserts trust itself; it performs an authentication and records that it happened.

The user verified is always the caller's own, taken from the peer credentials of the connection rather than from a claimed name, so a process may only verify itself. The service drives PAM and therefore runs privileged. It announces readiness through sd_notify3 and terminates cleanly on SIGTERM.

refsect1.title: The Varlink interface
refsect1.para: The service exposes a single varlink7 interface, io.platformd.Verify, on a AF_UNIX socket at /run/platformd-verifyd/io.platformd.Verify. Its one method, VerifyUser, takes the session to refresh and a human-readable reason, runs the PAM stack, and returns whether the user was verified together with the PAM service that ran. On success the verification is recorded with the trust authority. No secret material crosses the interface.

refsect1.title: Factors
refsect1.para: The factors offered are the auth lines of the platformd-verify PAM stack (/usr/lib/pam.d/platformd-verify, overridable under /etc/pam.d/). Any PAM authentication module may be used — fingerprint (pam_fprintd.so), face, a security key (pam_u2f.so), or a password (pam_unix.so); the service does not privilege any of them. The first to succeed verifies presence.

Hardware factors are prompted by their own device — the reader or key is the prompt — and need no interactive agent. A knowledge factor such as a password requires a prompt to be rendered in the user's session, which needs a prompt agent that is not yet available; such factors are declined until it is. The reported method names the PAM service, not the individual factor.
